html:
The Livonian Brothers of the Sword were a crusading order of German knights founded in 1202 by Albert, Bishop of Riga, to conquer and convert the pagan peoples of the eastern Baltic.

Albert had founded Riga the year before. Over thirty years the knights conquered the Livs, Latvians and Estonians in brutal campaigns. In 1236 the Lithuanians and Semigallians destroyed their army at the battle of Saule, and the survivors joined the Teutonic Order the next year as the Livonian Order.

The conquest, part of the Northern Crusades, created Livonia, ruled by German bishops, knights and towns. A German-speaking upper class kept most of the land in what are now Latvia and Estonia until the 20th century.
sum: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword were a crusading order of German knights founded in 1202 by Albert, Bishop of Riga, to conquer and convert the pagan peoples of the eastern Baltic.
